title: Pin the foot of a five-bar robot leg
instruction: Join the robot leg's two lower links at the foot so the orange stud clicks into the blue jaw, then let go.
context: Robot building: legged robots are assembled, and repaired after falls, by pinning the two lower links of each five-bar leg together at the foot, a step robots must take over for robot production and upkeep to scale. With the motors off the leg is two passive two-joint chains hanging from hip bearings 100 mm apart (the textbook five-bar layout; Minitaur and Doggo put both hips on one axis). Neither foot reaches the other at full stretch, and a push on one chain only swings it away, so each arm must bend its own chain along that chain's joint path into the leg's diamond, and the two press the stud into the jaw against each other. Unlike TK-K65XCN (connectors on loose cords) or TK-CGNU3G (two halves set down together), nothing here is fixed and nothing lifts free: each end hangs on its own jointed chain and gives way.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. Every bearing axis runs along x (the leg's plane faces the robot), and all joints turn freely (0.002 N m Coulomb friction, limits +-150 deg). (1) Hip block and stand: grey aluminium, sRGB (0.62, 0.64, 0.67), 1.5 kg, fixed to the table: a 40 x 170 x 45 mm block centred at (0.342, 0.000, 1.005) on a 30 x 40 x 235 mm post centred at (0.345, 0.000, 0.865) and a 90 x 160 x 8 mm foot centred at (0.365, 0.000, 0.7515). Two steel hip axles (8 mm) at (0.300, +-0.050, 1.0025), 255 mm above the table; the block and stand sit behind the links, out of the leg's plane. (2) Two thighs: black 3D-printed PLA, sRGB (0.10, 0.10, 0.11), 40 g each, 8 x 16 x 91 mm (75 mm bearing to bearing); left at x 0.285, right at x 0.315; hanging straight down from the hips, centres (0.285, 0.050, 0.965) and (0.315, -0.050, 0.965). (3) Two shins: carbon-fibre plate, sRGB (0.20, 0.20, 0.22), 8 x 12 mm section, 110 mm from the knee bearing (z 0.9275) to the foot point (z 0.8175); left at x 0.295 (122 mm long, 38 g with its stud), right at x 0.305 (105 mm of bar, 42 g with its jaw). They hang straight down, feet 100 mm apart and 70 mm above the table. (4) Stud: orange steel, sRGB (0.95, 0.45, 0.05), 8 mm diameter, 11.5 mm long along x from the left shin's back face, with a 14 mm x 3 mm head, at the left foot point (0.304, 0.050, 0.8175). (5) Jaw: blue anodised aluminium, sRGB (0.15, 0.35, 0.85), on the right shin's foot end around the foot point (0.305, -0.050, 0.8175), 8 mm thick: a 9 x 9 mm pocket (0.5 mm play around the stud) whose mouth faces the leg's inside, 46 deg off the shin toward its foot end (toward +y and 44 deg down while hanging; straight toward +y in the leg's closing pose), with a 16 mm guide lip on one side and a 45 deg lead-in on its end. (6) Latch tongue: spring steel, sRGB (0.75, 0.76, 0.78), 3 g, a 20 x 1.5 x 7 mm strip with a 12 mm 45 deg lead-in, sliding across the mouth on a 100 N/m spring with 1.0 N preload (10 mm travel); its tip sits 2.5 mm past the pocket centre and clicks shut behind the stud.
scoring: Measured from link poses every control step from reset: the stud's centre in the jaw frame (mm from the pocket centre, along the mouth and across it) and the tongue's travel from its stop. Snapped: the stud's centre within 1.5 mm of the pocket centre and the tongue back within 1.0 mm of its stop. Held: a gripper open at most 30 mm with a pad within 4 mm of the shin. Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset, so pulling the foot apart again never clears an earlier rung). Ladder: 0.25 = both shins held, each by its own gripper, with the stud within 10 mm of the jaw centre at some time; 0.5 = snapped at some time; 0.75 = snapped at the end; 1.0 = snapped for the last 1 s and the release gate: every pad of both grippers at least 30 mm from every part of the leg and both grippers moving under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. Real trial: a feeler gauge and a look through the jaw's mouth for the stud home and the tongue across it, a tape for the gripper clearance, and the video for stillness.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Push the tongue back with a fingernail, lift the stud out of the jaw and let both chains hang straight down at rest (feet 100 mm apart, about 70 mm above the table). Check that the tongue springs back across the mouth. The hip block and stand are fixed on a taped outline and need no reset.
fidelity: Rigid plates on free bearings (0.002 N m) and a contact snap: a sprung tongue on a slider clicks over the stud. Real five-bar feet use a shoulder bolt and nut, and Minitaur and Doggo put both hip motors on one axis; here the hip bearings are 100 mm apart so each arm works its own side. The latch is light (1.0 N preload) to suit the arms' soft position control. No motors, cables or feet pads are fitted.
